symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Generic tier index; \(K+1\) denotes the unconstrained tier.

symbols.name: \theta
symbols.def: Homogeneous effect of the exposure on the outcome.

symbols.name: q_0
symbols.def: Generic cutoff at which the finite-root and directional-tail certificates are constructed.

symbols.name: q^+
symbols.def: A rational number satisfying \(q^+\ge q\) and \(\Pr\{\chi^2_{2p}>q^+\}\le\alpha\).

symbols.name: \bar q
symbols.def: \(\bar q\) is the positive rational exact-arithmetic cutoff to be supplied by the worked audit construction and has no confidence-level interpretation.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_K)\) requires at least \(b_k\) violations to have magnitude at most \(\tau_k\).

symbols.name: \beta_{X,j}
symbols.def: Population instrument--exposure association for instrument \(j\), with no lower bound on its magnitude.

symbols.name: B_j
symbols.def: Known within-pair outcome--exposure covariance in block \(j\), permitted to be nonzero for correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries; genuinely independent disjoint two-sample summaries satisfy \(B_j=0\).

symbols.name: \Sigma_j
symbols.def: Fixed covariance scale for block \(j\) in the triangular block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment.

symbols.name: \gamma
symbols.def: Reduced-form violation vector satisfying \(\gamma_j=\beta_{Y,j}-\theta\beta_{X,j}\) at effect \(\theta\).

symbols.name: \Gamma
symbols.def: Nested BudgetIV violation set constructed in \(\mathrm{def:budget\text{-}set}\).

symbols.name: E_q
symbols.def: Joint Gaussian confidence ellipsoid constructed in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}ellipsoid}\).

symbols.name: C_{\alpha}^+
symbols.def: Conservative exact-arithmetic complex obtained by replacing \(q\) with \(q^+\) in \(C_{\alpha}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal B
symbols.type: finite subset of the real line
symbols.def: Hinge and exchange-cycle structural breakpoints constructed in \(\mathrm{def:exchange\text{-}partition}\).

symbols.name: N_{j,k,\sigma}
symbols.def: For \(k\le K\), \(N_{j,k,\sigma}(t)=(|\widehat\beta_{X,j}|-t(\sigma\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_{X,j})\widehat\beta_{Y,j}+\tau_k))^2\) when \(\widehat\beta_{X,j}\ne0\), and \(N_{j,k,\sigma}(t)=t^2(|\widehat\beta_{Y,j}|-\tau_k)_+^2\) otherwise; set \(N_{j,K+1,\sigma}=0\).

symbols.name: \ell(q_0)
symbols.def: \(\ell(q_0)=\bigl(\prod_{j=1}^{p}D_j\bigr)(L-q_0)\), the common constant coefficient after reciprocal-tail denominator clearing.

symbols.name: \lambda_{\sigma}(q_0)
symbols.def: Coefficient vector, in ascending powers of \(t\), of the lexicographically smallest polynomial among \(\{P_{a,\sigma}^{(q_0)}:a\in\mathcal A\}\), computed by additive lexicographic min-cost flow; its zeroth coordinate is \(\ell(q_0)\).

symbols.name: \mathcal I_{\mathrm{audit}}
symbols.def: A rational \(p=3\), \(K=2\) BudgetIV instance to be derived by the construction handle in \(\mathrm{def:rational\text{-}audit\text{-}instance}\).

symbols.name: \mathsf{AlgInput}
symbols.def: Predicate constructed in \(\mathrm{def:algebraic\text{-}input\text{-}domain}\) requiring every load-bearing coefficient input for the \(q^+\) branch to be rational or real algebraic.

symbols.name: \nu_e
symbols.def: At a regular endpoint \(e\) generated by \(\beta_{Y,j}-e\beta_{X,j}=s\tau_k\), let \(\nu_e=\operatorname{sign}(-s\beta_{X,j})\).

symbols.name: \widetilde e_n
symbols.def: Boundary point of \(C_{\alpha}\) paired with a population regular endpoint \(e\) under the local Gaussian scaling.

symbols.name: \mathsf{CertInv}
symbols.def: Algorithmic object specified by the exchange-cycle and real-root-isolation handle in \(\mathrm{def:certified\text{-}inversion\text{-}handle}\).

assumptions.condition: \(\widehat W_j\sim N_2(W_j,\Omega_j)\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), where \(\Omega_j\in\mathbb S_{++}^{2}\) may have \(B_j\ne0\).

novel.justification: This model-specific exact Gaussian experiment directly permits correlated exposure--outcome coordinates within an instrument block, as arise from overlapping samples or correlated summary construction. It is an experiment restriction rather than a consequence attributed to an independent two-sample model.

This model-specific restriction concerns independence across instrument blocks and is plausible after stringent linkage-disequilibrium clumping. It permits correlated exposure--outcome coordinates within each block, while residual cross-instrument dependence lies outside the exact guarantee.

This model-specific calibration restriction is appropriate when covariance blocks are fixed by the sampling design or supplied as exact reference quantities; estimated standard errors do not inherit the exact finite-sample claim.

This model-specific triangular experiment is a transparent approximation for fixed-dimensional summary statistics whose covariance contracts at rate \(n^{-1}\); it is imposed directly and is not attributed as a consequence of a published weak-IV model.

standard.name: regular identification away from the weak boundary

assumptions.condition: There exist an integer \(R\ge1\), a margin \(\eta>0\), ordered intervals \([\ell_r,u_r]\), and endpoint labels \((a^e,j_e,k_e,s_e)\) such that \(\Theta_I=\bigcup_{r=1}^{R}[\ell_r,u_r]\), \(u_r-\ell_r\ge4\eta\), \(\ell_{r+1}-u_r\ge4\eta\), every finite endpoint \(e\) has \(a^e\in\mathcal A\) as its unique locally feasible exact-capacity assignment and \(j_e\) as its unique binding constrained instrument with \(k_e=a^e_{j_e}\le K\), \(s_e\in\{-1,+1\}\), and \(\beta_{Y,j_e}-e\beta_{X,j_e}=s_e\tau_{k_e}\), every other constrained edge satisfies \(\tau_{a^e_j}-|\beta_{Y,j}-e\beta_{X,j}|\ge\eta\), every \(a\ne a^e\) has a constrained edge with \(|\beta_{Y,j}-e\beta_{X,j}|-\tau_{a_j}\ge\eta\), uniformly for \(|\vartheta-e|\le\eta\) every nontrivial simple exchange cycle \((j_i,k_i)_{i=1}^{m}\) away from \(a^e\) obeys \(\left|\sum_{i=1}^{m}[\bar c_{j_i,k_{i+1}}(\vartheta)-\bar c_{j_i,k_i}(\vartheta)]\right|\ge\eta\) with \(k_{m+1}=k_1\), and the ordered endpoint labels remain the unique local labels on these neighborhoods and fix the pairing \((\ell_r,u_r)\).

novel.justification: For fixed \(p\) and \(K\), positive component widths, positive gaps, unique binding bands, and nonzero exchange reduced costs are finitely many strict inequalities. Under continuously varying reduced-form means they define open cells, while failures lie on endpoint-collision, tangency, or assignment-tie surfaces. The margin is observable in a population sensitivity analysis and isolates exactly the faces on which component labels have a stable interpretation.

definitions.name: \Gamma
inputs: The published BudgetIV thresholds \(\tau\) and cumulative counts \(b\).

definitions.name: \Theta_I
inputs: Population reduced-form means \(W_1,\ldots,W_p\) and budget set \(\Gamma\).

definitions.name: E_q
definitions.construction: \[E_q=\left\{(u_j,v_j)_{j=1}^{p}:\sum_{j=1}^{p}((u_j,v_j)^{\mathsf T}-\widehat W_j)^{\mathsf T}\Omega_j^{-1}((u_j,v_j)^{\mathsf T}-\widehat W_j)\le q\right\}.\]
inputs: Observed blocks \(\widehat W_j\), covariance blocks \(\Omega_j\), and cutoff \(q\).

definitions.name: M
inputs: Observed reduced-form pairs, covariance blocks, and the assignment family \(\mathcal A\).

definitions.name: C(q_0), C_{\alpha}, C_{\alpha}^+
definitions.construction: \[C(q_0)=\{\theta\in\mathbb R:M(\theta)\le q_0\},\qquad C_{\alpha}=C(q)=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R:\exists (u,v)\in E_q,\ (u_j-\theta v_j)_{j=1}^{p}\in\Gamma\right\},\qquad C_{\alpha}^+=C(q^+).\]
inputs: BudgetIV envelope \(M\), generic cutoff \(q_0\), exact Gaussian cutoff \(q\), and rational conservative cutoff \(q^+\).

definitions.name: \mathcal N(\theta)
definitions.construction: Create a source, instrument nodes \(j\), bin nodes \(k\), and a sink; give each source-to-instrument arc capacity one and cost zero, each instrument-to-bin arc capacity one and cost \(c_{j,k}(\theta)\), and each bin-to-sink arc capacity \(d_k\) and cost zero; require a flow of value \(p\).
inputs: The cost matrix \(c_{j,k}(\theta)\) and exact bin capacities \(d_k\).

definitions.name: \mathcal B
definitions.construction: Take every finite hinge root \(r_j(\theta)=\pm\tau_k\). On each resulting hinge cell, for every simple exchange cycle through distinct bins \(k_1,\ldots,k_m\) and distinct instruments \(j_1,\ldots,j_m\), where \(2\le m\le K+1\), clear the positive denominators in \(\sum_{i=1}^{m}[c_{j_i,k_{i+1}}(\theta)-c_{j_i,k_i}(\theta)]\) with \(k_{m+1}=k_1\), and add every real zero of the resulting polynomial to \(\mathcal B\).

definitions.name: (L,\ell(q_0),\lambda_{-1}(q_0),\lambda_{+1}(q_0))
definitions.construction: For an arbitrary \(q_0>0\), compute \(L\) from the \(b_K\) smallest values of \(\widehat\beta_{X,j}^2/D_j\) and set \(\ell(q_0)=(\prod_{j=1}^{p}D_j)(L-q_0)\). For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,+1\}\), form \(Q_{j,\sigma}\), \(N_{j,k,\sigma}\), and \(P_{a,\sigma}^{(q_0)}\), then minimize the ascending coefficient vectors over \(a\in\mathcal A\) by additive lexicographic min-cost flow to obtain the complete equality-case certificate \(\lambda_{\sigma}(q_0)\). Instantiate this construction separately at \(q_0=q\) and \(q_0=q^+\).
inputs: Observed summaries, covariance blocks, budget inputs, and an arbitrary cutoff \(q_0\), instantiated independently at \(q\) and \(q^+\).

definitions.name: \mathsf{AlgInput}
definitions.construction: \[\mathsf{AlgInput}\Longleftrightarrow q^+,\ \tau_k,\ \widehat\beta_{Y,j},\ \widehat\beta_{X,j},\ A_j,\ B_j,\ D_j\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\cap\mathbb R\text{ for every }j\le p\text{ and }k\le K,\quad b_k\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }k\le K.\] Thus the requirement explicitly covers the cutoff, every tier threshold and budget, both observed summaries, and every covariance entry used in a boundary coefficient.
inputs: The complete numeric input tuple for the conservative \(q^+\) inversion branch.

definitions.name: \mathcal I_{\mathrm{audit}}
definitions.construction: Handle: construct rational data with \(p=3\), \(K=2\), a strict rational tier vector \(0\le\tau_1<\tau_2\), exact capacities induced by \(b=(1,2)\), positive-definite rational covariance blocks, and a positive rational cutoff \(\bar q\). First impose the exact equality-tail equation \(L=\bar q\). Then tune the remaining rational summaries and covariance entries so that a nontrivial simple exchange-cycle reduced-cost polynomial changes sign within one hinge cell. The output must give all coefficients, isolating intervals, optimizer witnesses on both sides of that cycle root, the first nonzero coordinate and sign of each \(\lambda_{\sigma}(\bar q)\), and an exhaustive check over all six exact-capacity assignments.
inputs: No external input; deriving explicit rational coefficients and their complete certificate is an open validation obligation.

definitions.name: \mathsf{CertInv}
definitions.construction: Handle: for a supplied cutoff \(q_0\), combine exact nested-quota min-cost flow, exhaustive simple exchange-cycle sign cells, square-free factorization, Sturm or subresultant real-root isolation, endpoint sign determination, and the cutoff-specific certificate \(\{\ell(q_0),\lambda_{-1}(q_0),\lambda_{+1}(q_0)\}\) to construct an output-sensitive list of all accepted intervals, singleton tangencies, and rays. Run the full construction separately with \(q_0=q\) and \(q_0=q^+\).
inputs: For \(q\), arbitrary real-valued thresholds, summaries, and covariance entries together with exact-real sign oracles; for unconditional bit arithmetic at \(q^+\), the full tuple must satisfy \(\mathsf{AlgInput}\).

statements.statement: The published nested budget set has the exact union representation \[\Gamma=\bigcup_{a\in\mathcal A}\left\{\gamma\in\mathbb R^p:|\gamma_j|\le\tau_{a_j}\text{ whenever }a_j\le K\right\}.\] Exact bin counts impose no lower bound on a violation assigned to a looser tier.
statements.justification: The union identity is the exact bridge from nested magnitude counts to a balanced discrete assignment problem.
statements.gap: Penn et al. characterize the budget union, but the exact-capacity form needed for the Gaussian distance and flow certificate is not their inferential construction.
statements.consumer: The distance theorem and every component label use this representation without enumerating overlapping budget witnesses.

statements.statement: For every \(\theta\in\mathbb R\), the squared Mahalanobis distance from \((\widehat W_j)_{j=1}^{p}\) to the set of reduced-form means satisfying \((u_j-\theta v_j)_{j=1}^{p}\in\Gamma\) equals \(M(\theta)\). In particular, \(C_{\alpha}=\{\theta:M(\theta)\le q\}\), including arbitrary known within-pair covariance \(B_j\), as can arise from correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries, and zero observed or population first stages. Genuinely independent disjoint two-sample exposure--outcome summaries are exactly the submodel \(B_j=0\).
statements.justification: This formula turns a nonconvex projection in \(2p\) reduced-form coordinates into a one-dimensional lower envelope with interpretable quota assignments.
statements.gap: Dufour and Taamouti project one quadric, while VIPER profiles a general violation set; neither derives the separable graded-quota envelope with exposure-association uncertainty.
statements.consumer: The formula supplies the computable objective for the complete inversion algorithm and for covariance-aware BudgetIV analysis of overlapping or correlated GWAS summary pairs, with disjoint two-sample analyses obtained by setting \(B_j=0\).

statements.statement: For fixed \(p\) and fixed finite \(K\), the single projected complex uniformly contains the entire population identified set in the block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment with known covariance: \[\inf_{(W_1,\ldots,W_p)\in(\mathbb R^2)^p}\Pr_W\{\Theta_I(W;\Gamma)\subseteq C_{\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Blocks are independent across instruments, whereas \(B_j\) may be nonzero within a block; the genuinely independent disjoint two-sample exposure--outcome model is the submodel \(B_j=0\). The bound holds at exactly zero, local-to-zero, or strong first stages and for empty, connected, disconnected, or unbounded realizations of the projected complex. Relative to Penn et al.'s NOME asymptotic construction, this is a strict strengthening only within that experiment because it propagates uncertainty in both reduced forms and controls one simultaneous whole-set event. It is not an exact guarantee with estimated covariance blocks, residual linkage disequilibrium, SNP selection, or a Gaussian approximation to GWAS summary statistics.
statements.justification: A whole-set event is stronger than coverage of one unknown effect and remains meaningful when the same population reduced form supports multiple separated effects.
statements.gap: Penn et al. give NOME-based asymptotic inference and VIPER Proposition 2 gives pointwise strong validity for the true effect; neither states this exact simultaneous containment event for BudgetIV under uncertainty in both reduced forms.
statements.consumer: An analyst with known covariance for overlapping or correlated exposure--outcome summaries can report every BudgetIV component under one joint guarantee; a disjoint two-sample analysis uses the \(B_j=0\) specialization.

statements.statement: For each \(\theta\), every integral flow of value \(p\) in \(\mathcal N(\theta)\) is in bijection with one \(a\in\mathcal A\), preserves total cost, and has minimum cost \(M(\theta)\). The network therefore yields an exact polynomial-time oracle in \(p\) and \(K\) at a fixed parameter value.
statements.justification: The bijection rules out the balance-sign and uncoupled-sorting errors that invalidate naive quota optimization.
statements.gap: Orlin supplies the generic min-cost-flow algorithm, but the correctly balanced laminar encoding of BudgetIV tiers and its assignment interpretation are new to this target.
statements.consumer: This oracle replaces exponential assignment enumeration inside exact confidence-set inversion.

statements.statement: For fixed \(K\) and arbitrary real-valued tier thresholds, observed summaries, and covariance entries forming positive-definite blocks, the set \(\mathcal B\) contains \(O_K(p^{K+1})\) structural breakpoints and fixes at least one globally optimal assignment on every connected component of \(\mathbb R\setminus\mathcal B\). Clearing positive denominators for that assignment produces boundary polynomials of degree at most \(2p\). At \(q_0=q\), exact root isolation, equality-complete finite-root signs, and the tail certificate \(\{\ell(q),\lambda_{-1}(q),\lambda_{+1}(q)\}\) enumerate every component of \(C_{\alpha}\), including closed bounded intervals, singleton tangencies, closed rays, \(\varnothing\), and \(\mathbb R\), with no user-supplied search window; termination is relative to exact-real sign oracles for the arbitrary-real coefficients and \(q\), and this branch imposes no rationality or algebraicity restriction. Separately, if \(\mathsf{AlgInput}\) holds, then at \(q_0=q^+\) the boundary polynomials and the distinct tail certificate \(\{\ell(q^+),\lambda_{-1}(q^+),\lambda_{+1}(q^+)\}\) enumerate every component of \(C_{\alpha}^+\) by unconditional terminating exact arithmetic. This hypothesis covers every tier threshold \(\tau_k\), every integer budget \(b_k\), both observed summaries for every instrument, every covariance entry \(A_j,B_j,D_j\), and \(q^+\). In the all-rational subcase, writing \(S=|\mathcal B|+1=O_K(p^{K+1})\) for the realized cell count and \(H\) for the maximum bit length of this complete numeric input after primitive integer normalization, a Sturm implementation uses \(S\) min-cost-flow certificates on networks of size \(O(pK)\), \(\widetilde O(S(2p)^4H^2)\) bit operations for the degree-at-most-\(2p\) cell-boundary isolations, and linear work in the serialized list of accepted components. The singleton-assignment rational-statistic inversion of Schlemper and Moreira is a special case, whereas completeness of the non-singleton graded-quota exchange-cycle partition and its equality cases is a strict addition.
statements.justification: Completeness at ties, tangencies, isolated points, and infinity is the computational content needed to make a disconnected weak-IV confidence object trustworthy.
statements.gap: Schlemper and Moreira isolate roots for one rational or polynomial weak-IV statistic; this theorem strictly adds a quota-constrained lower envelope and proves that all optimizer changes are captured by bounded-length exchange cycles.
statements.consumer: The result prevents missed BudgetIV components and truncated rays in the 48-pair GWAS sensitivity analysis.

statements.statement: For every cutoff \(q_0>0\), both directional limits satisfy \(\lim_{\theta\to+\infty}M(\theta)=\lim_{\theta\to-\infty}M(\theta)=L\), and the leading cleared coefficient is \(\ell(q_0)=(\prod_{j=1}^{p}D_j)(L-q_0)\). If \(\ell(q_0)<0\), both rays belong eventually to \(C(q_0)\); if \(\ell(q_0)>0\), \(C(q_0)\) is bounded. If \(\ell(q_0)=0\), the \(\sigma\)-ray belongs eventually if and only if \(\lambda_{\sigma}(q_0)=0\) or the first nonzero coordinate of \(\lambda_{\sigma}(q_0)\) is negative. This complete lexicographic decision agrees with eventual exact inversion for every tie pattern, including \(\widehat\beta_{X,j}=0\). Thus \(C_{\alpha}=C(q)\) uses \(\lambda_{\sigma}(q)\), while the independently certified conservative complex \(C_{\alpha}^+=C(q^+)\) uses \(\lambda_{\sigma}(q^+)\). For \(p=K=b_1=1\) and \(\tau_1=0\), the criterion reduces to Fieller's leading-coefficient classification; nontrivial nested quotas strictly add trimmed order statistics and lexicographic assignment resolution.
statements.justification: The theorem characterizes exactly when honest weak-stage uncertainty must appear as one or two infinite tails rather than as a numerical artifact.
statements.gap: Fieller and Mikusheva classify denominator-driven tails for one statistic; the nested-quota order statistic and its equality-case lexicographic recursion are absent from those classifications.
statements.consumer: The inversion backend can certify rays without evaluating the statistic at an arbitrary large grid endpoint.

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal C(\widehat W)\subseteq\mathbb R\) be any measurable procedure satisfying \(\inf_W\Pr_W\{\Theta_I(W;\Gamma)\subseteq\mathcal C(\widehat W)\}\ge1-\alpha>0\). Then \(\mathcal C\) cannot be almost surely bounded under every Gaussian mean law. At \(W_j=0\) for all \(j\), it equals \(\mathbb R\) with probability at least \(1-\alpha\); along nonzero local sequences \(\beta_{X,j}=h_j/\theta_m^2\), \(\beta_{Y,j}=h_j/\theta_m\), and \(\theta_m\to\infty\), uniform positive coverage is incompatible with almost-sure boundedness.
statements.justification: The lower bound explains why unbounded components are required by honesty rather than caused by a defective algorithm.
statements.gap: Dufour proves the general locally almost unidentified impossibility; this lemma records its BudgetIV specialization only as inherited supporting context and makes no novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Reviewers and applied users obtain a formal reason not to trim remote components or rays for presentation.

statements.statement: In the triangular block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, under the primitive model-specific BudgetIV regular-face condition and only on that domain, \(C_{\alpha}\) recovers with probability tending to one the number, order, stable pairing, and unique active assignment--instrument--tier labels of the connected components of \(\Theta_I\). The within-pair covariance in \(\Sigma_j\) may be nonzero. If a labeled population endpoint \(e\) is generated by the unique \(j\), \(k\), and \(s\in\{-1,+1\}\) satisfying \(\beta_{Y,j}-e\beta_{X,j}=s\tau_k\), then jointly over all finite endpoints, \[\sqrt n(\widetilde e_n-e)\;\Rightarrow\;\frac{Z_{Y,j}-eZ_{X,j}}{\beta_{X,j}}+\nu_e\frac{\sqrt q\,\sqrt{v_j(e)}}{|\beta_{X,j}|}.\] No endpoint, component, pairing, or label-recovery conclusion is asserted outside this domain; in particular the theorem excludes zero population first stages, tangencies, shrinking widths or gaps, exchange ties, singleton components, and all nonregular faces.
statements.justification: Whole-set coverage alone does not justify interpreting individual endpoints or assignment labels, so a regular-face limit theorem marks the exact interpretability region.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer give set-level convergence, and Gafarov gives regularized limits for affine polygon bounds; neither recovers labeled components of a disconnected quota envelope with outward ellipsoid shifts.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers can attach asymptotic uncertainty and stable invalidity-tier interpretations to each separated BudgetIV component.

statements.statement: For every sign vector \(g\in\{-1,+1\}^{p}\), replacing \(W_j\) and \(\widehat W_j\) by \(g_jW_j\) and \(g_j\widehat W_j\), and conjugating any non-diagonal cross-coordinate representation accordingly, leaves \(\Theta_I\), \(M\), \(C_{\alpha}\), the tail decisions, and the component assignment labels invariant after the same sign action.
statements.justification: Equivalent SNP allele codings must not alter either causal conclusions or the topology of a reported confidence complex.
statements.gap: Lin, Pan, and Pan document coding dependence of MR--Egger, while Dudbridge et al. repair a different directional-pleiotropy model; this direct sign-action identity is retained only as a validation lemma.
statements.consumer: The published 48-pair recoding study obtains a falsifiable invariance benchmark for covariance-aware magnitude-budget inference, using \(B_j=0\) for genuinely disjoint exposure--outcome samples and supplied nonzero \(B_j\) for overlapping summaries.

statements.statement: When \(K=1\), \(b_1=p\), and \(\tau_1=0\), the assignment family is a singleton and \(M(\theta)=\sum_{j=1}^{p}(\widehat\beta_{Y,j}-\theta\widehat\beta_{X,j})^2/(A_j-2B_j\theta+D_j\theta^2)\). For \(p=1\), clearing the single positive quadratic denominator gives the classical Fieller quadratic inversion. For \(p>1\), the faithful reduction is the Anderson--Rubin-type sum of rational terms; after multiplication by \(\prod_{j=1}^{p}(A_j-2B_j\theta+D_j\theta^2)\), its boundary polynomial has degree at most \(2p\), and it is not generally a Fieller quadratic. In every dimension the joint-ellipsoid construction retains the conservative cutoff \(q_{1-\alpha}(\chi^2_{2p})\) rather than claiming pointwise \(\chi^2_p\) efficiency.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check and makes the price of simultaneous whole-set projection explicit.
statements.gap: Wang and Kang provide pointwise weak-IV robust tests; this definitional reduction is only a sanity lemma, makes no power claim, and locates the exact overlap.
statements.consumer: Users can benchmark \(p=1\) against classical Fieller inversion and \(p>1\) against direct evaluation of the all-valid Anderson--Rubin-type rational statistic.

statements.statement: Can one derive an explicit nontrivial rational \(p=3\), \(K=2\) instance \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{audit}}\) and a machine-readable certificate at cutoff \(\bar q\) that exhibit all three required validation events: a sign-changing simple exchange cycle that changes the optimal quota assignment, the equality-tail case \(L=\bar q\) resolved by the first nonzero coordinate of each \(\lambda_{\sigma}(\bar q)\), and exact agreement of all cells, boundary roots, intervals, singleton points, endpoints, labels, and rays with exhaustive inversion over the six exact-capacity assignments? Can one then construct \(\mathsf{CertInv}\) so that the same agreement holds on one hundred rational instances with \(p\le6\) and \(K\le2\), and prove it for every fixed-\(K\) input satisfying \(\mathsf{AlgInput}\) while retaining polynomial delay in the number of structural cells and isolated roots?
statements.justification: The theorem becomes usable only when the exchange-cycle partition and boundary certificates are executable and adversarially checked as complete objects.
statements.gap: Schlemper and Moreira implement polynomial inversion for ordinary statistics, and Orlin certifies a fixed min-cost flow; neither supplies an equality-complete parametric quota-envelope backend.
statements.consumer: Producing the still-open explicit \(p=3\), \(K=2\) certificate and passing the prespecified one-hundred-instance kill test are the launch conditions for a reliable paired-summary BudgetIV implementation and the 48-pair \(B_j=0\) reanalysis.

sampling_model.design: Block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment with fixed \(p\) and fixed finite \(K\).
sampling_model.units: Instrument-indexed reduced-form pairs \(\widehat W_j=(\widehat\beta_{Y,j},\widehat\beta_{X,j})^{\mathsf T}\), mutually independent across instruments \(j\), with known positive-definite within-pair covariance \(\Omega_j\).
sampling_model.treatment: Scalar exposure with homogeneous scalar causal effect \(\theta\); population violations satisfy \(\gamma_j=\beta_{Y,j}-\theta\beta_{X,j}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summary samples are permitted within instrument \(j\) through arbitrary known \(B_j\) subject to \(\Omega_j\succ0\). Genuinely independent disjoint two-sample GWAS summaries are exactly the submodel \(B_j=0\).
sampling_model.first_stage: No lower bound is imposed on \(|\beta_{X,j}|\); exactly zero and local-to-zero first stages are included in the finite-sample coverage theorem.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The covariance blocks \(\Omega_j\), including any nonzero within-pair covariance \(B_j\), are known. Estimated covariance, cross-instrument dependence, SNP selection, and non-Gaussian approximation are outside the exact theorem.
sampling_model.asymptotic_submodel: For endpoint limits only, \(\Omega_j=\Sigma_j/n\) with fixed positive-definite \(\Sigma_j\), nonzero population first stages, and the primitive model-specific regular-face domain with positive widths and gaps, unique active labels, stable pairing, and a positive exchange-cycle margin.

estimand_functional: \(C_{\alpha}=\{\theta\in\mathbb R:M(\theta)\le q_{1-\alpha}(\chi^2_{2p})\}\), where \(M(\theta)=\min_{a\in\mathcal A}\sum_{j=1}^{p}c_{j,a_j}(\theta)\), \(c_{j,k}(\theta)=(|\widehat\beta_{Y,j}-\theta\widehat\beta_{X,j}|-\tau_k)_+^2/(A_j-2B_j\theta+D_j\theta^2)\) for \(k\le K\), and \(c_{j,K+1}(\theta)=0\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: BudgetIV gives a sharp, possibly disconnected finite union under nested magnitude-count budgets and asymptotic inference under NOME.
Polynomial and rational weak-IV statistics can be inverted without a grid by isolating all real boundary roots and determining signs between them.
Gaussian ratio inversion can produce bounded, complement, or unbounded confidence sets according to the quadratic coefficients.
Exact validification yields finite-sample pointwise coverage for the true structural effect when the true violation lies in the posited set.
Projection of an Anderson--Rubin quadric gives weak-identification-robust confidence sets and an analytic boundedness classification.
Any valid confidence set for an unbounded locally almost unidentified parameter must be unbounded with positive probability.
Regularized support-function estimators have Gaussian limits under regular affine geometry and remain consistent in nonregular cases.

tldr: The field-level kernel is a new completeness theorem for a graded-quota lower envelope: balanced min-cost flow, every simple exchange cycle, and equality-complete polynomial sign decomposition together enumerate every BudgetIV interval, singleton, and ray without a bounded grid. In the fixed-\(p\), fixed-finite-\(K\), block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment with known covariance, projection of one joint ellipsoid also gives finite-sample uniform containment of the entire population identified set, while a cutoff-indexed trimmed first-stage statistic and lexicographic certificate resolve both tails separately at \(q\) and \(q^+\). Arbitrary known \(B_j\) permits correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries within each instrument; genuinely independent disjoint two-sample GWAS is exactly the submodel \(B_j=0\). This exact coverage is not a guarantee for estimated covariance or residual linkage disequilibrium; exact-\(q\) termination is oracle-relative for arbitrary-real inputs, while unconditional conservative arithmetic at \(q^+\) requires every threshold, budget, observed summary, covariance entry, and \(q^+\) used in boundary coefficients to be rational or real algebraic and rebuilds the finite-root and tail certificates at that cutoff; endpoint and label recovery is confined to the primitive positive-width regular-face domain with stable pairing, unique active labels, and a positive exchange-cycle margin, excluding zero first stages, tangencies, shrinking gaps, exchange ties, singletons, and other nonregular components.

project_justification.gap: Penn et al. leave inference without NOME open; pointwise weak-IV and invalid-IV procedures do not supply simultaneous containment of a disconnected BudgetIV population set; and root-based ordinary-IV inversion does not handle a lower envelope over nested quota assignments.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is an exact weak-stage, covariance-aware confidence complex for the published BudgetIV set in a block-independent paired-summary Gaussian experiment, together with a sound-and-complete combinatorial--algebraic topology certificate.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the projection cost and whole-set coverage inside the block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, allowing known within-pair covariance from correlated or overlapping summaries and specializing to disjoint two-sample summaries at \(B_j=0\). It then makes the quota-flow exchange-cycle completeness and equality-complete certified topology inversion the field-level result. The first open validation deliverable is an explicit rational \(p=3\), \(K=2\) certificate exhibiting an optimizer-changing cycle, an equality-tail decision, and exhaustive-assignment agreement, followed by a one-hundred-instance comparison.

related_work: Penn et al. (2025, Sections 3--4 and 6--7) provide the writing model: invalidity budgets lead to interpretable disconnected sharp sets, and their discussion names non-NOME finite-sample uncertainty as open. Dufour and Taamouti (2005) provide the projection and quadric geometry adapted here, but only for one structural confidence region. Wang and Kang (2022, Theorem 1) establish weak-instrument-robust tests for genuinely independent two-sample summary associations, which correspond here to the \(B_j=0\) submodel; they assume valid instruments and target pointwise nulls, whereas the main paired-summary experiment also permits known \(B_j\ne0\) from correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries. Kang et al. (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 3) union confidence intervals over invalid subsets; their count restriction neither represents graded magnitude tiers nor proves simultaneous containment of every effect in one population set. Schlemper and Moreira (2026, Sections 4--7) motivate exact inversion by showing that grids miss components and rays; their root-and-sign method is adapted only after the new exchange-cycle partition freezes a quota optimizer. VIPER (Steiner, Houssineau, and Steel, 2026, Proposition 2 and Corollary 1) proves exact pointwise validification under a user-specified violation set and therefore blocks any claim to first finite-sample invalid-IV inference; its probability-integral-transform theorem is not a whole-identified-set containment theorem. Fieller (1954) and Mikusheva (2010) motivate honest unbounded sets, while Dufour (1997) supplies the supporting impossibility mechanism. Gafarov (2025) and Fang and Santos (2019) provide general regular and directionally differentiable context; the positive-width, stable-label, and positive exchange-cycle-margin condition is a primitive model-specific BudgetIV domain and is not attributed to either paper. Lin, Pan, and Pan (2022) supply the 48-pair coding-instability consumer for a disjoint-summary study, and Dudbridge et al. (2025) give a coding-invariant comparator under a different pleiotropy model.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact finite-sample theorem is conditional on fixed \(p\), fixed finite \(K\), the block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, and known positive-definite within-pair covariance. It permits \(B_j\ne0\) for correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries, while genuinely independent disjoint two-sample summaries are exactly the submodel \(B_j=0\). It is not an exact estimated-covariance, residual-linkage-disequilibrium, SNP-selection, or non-Gaussian GWAS guarantee. Dense cross-instrument covariance destroys the separable band cost because whitening rotates the quota set. Exact inversion at \(q\) permits arbitrary-real inputs but terminates only relative to exact-real sign oracles. Unconditional terminating arithmetic applies only to the enlarged conservative complex when every load-bearing threshold, integer budget, observed summary, covariance entry, and \(q^+\) is rational or real algebraic, after rebuilding both the finite-root signs and the complete lexicographic tail certificate at \(q^+\); the certificate frozen at \(q\) cannot certify \(C_{\alpha}^+\). The exchange-cycle count is polynomial only for fixed \(K\), and the constant can be impractical.
honest_scope: The field-level open content is the complete quota-flow exchange-cycle partition, equality-complete boundary-isolation certificate, and proof of agreement with exhaustive semialgebraic inversion. Its first explicit validation obligation is to derive, rather than presume, a rational \(p=3\), \(K=2\) certificate exhibiting a cycle-induced optimizer change, an equality-tail decision, and agreement with all six assignments, before testing one hundred small rational cases. Gaussian projection and simultaneous coverage are conditional finite-sample results only for fixed \(p\), fixed finite \(K\), the block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, and known covariance. The model permits known \(B_j\ne0\) within a block for correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries, and the genuinely independent disjoint two-sample GWAS model is exactly the \(B_j=0\) submodel; neither case transfers exactly to estimated covariance or residual linkage disequilibrium. Exact inversion at \(q\) accepts arbitrary-real inputs only through oracle-relative finite-root and tail signs. Unconditional conservative arithmetic at \(q^+\) requires the complete coefficient input tuple to be rational or real algebraic and uses separately instantiated \(q^+\)-specific certificates. Endpoint, component, pairing, and label recovery hold only on the primitive regular-face domain requiring positive widths and gaps, unique active quota assignments and bands, stable ordered labels, and a uniform positive exchange-cycle margin; zero first stages, tangencies, shrinking gaps, exchange ties, singleton or zero-width sets, and every other nonregular component are excluded. In the all-valid case, \(p=1\) gives Fieller's quadratic, while \(p>1\) gives only the Anderson--Rubin-type rational sum with a cleared boundary of degree at most \(2p\); the joint-ellipsoid cutoff is intentionally conservative for simultaneous containment.
seeds: regular-face endpoint and label limit law

seed_details.kernel: Derive the exact quota band-cost envelope, balanced min-cost flow, exchange-cycle structural partition, certified root inversion, and uniform containment of the entire BudgetIV population set.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After projecting each Gaussian block to a fixed violation band, ordinary polynomial inversion fails because the statistic is a lower envelope over quota assignments; the first new step is the exact assignment--flow bijection and exchange-cycle completeness theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from BudgetIV projection plus Schlemper--Moreira root finding because each assignment gives a rational statistic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The number of assignments is exponential, and neither source proves that all optimizer changes are generated by the enumerated bounded-length cycles or that one event covers every population-compatible effect simultaneously.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The object is an explicit evaluable envelope and certificate, not a bare projection or unspecified infimum.

seed_details.kernel: Give a necessary-and-sufficient two-sided ray criterion from the quota-trimmed first-stage order statistic and lexicographically ordered reciprocal-tail coefficient vectors at cutoff equality.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Fieller compares one leading quadratic coefficient; BudgetIV first requires minimizing leading and lower-order coefficients over nested quota assignments in an ordered additive group.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from taking the limit of every assignment cost because the assignment family is finite.
seed_details.rebuttal: The limit decides only strict inequalities; explicit legal examples with \(L=q\) yield the whole line, one ray, a bounded interval, or the empty set, so the lexicographic equality recursion is essential.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is an iff frontier with a named coefficient-vector certificate, not a qualitative statement that weak instruments cause rays.

seed_details.seed: regular-face endpoint and label limit law
seed_details.kernel: Derive the joint shifted Gaussian limit of every finite endpoint and consistent recovery of component pairing and assignment labels only on separated positive-width regular faces.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A set-consistency argument must be replaced by a local simple-root expansion with stable active assignment, followed by a global matching argument across separated components.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate delta method for ratios once endpoints are written as \((\beta_Y\pm\tau)/\beta_X\).
seed_details.rebuttal: The confidence endpoints are outward projections of an active lower envelope, so the shift, joint covariance, component matching, and failure at singleton or tie strata do not follow from ratio delta methods alone.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law, active-label recovery, and explicit nonregular frontier are all named.

seed_details.kernel: Project one exact joint Gaussian ellipsoid through the nested budget and prove uniform simultaneous containment of \(\Theta_I\).
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Pointwise weak-IV inversion is replaced by a common reduced-form ellipsoid event serving every \(\theta\in\Theta_I\).
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from the elementary projection principle.
seed_details.rebuttal: The coverage proof is elementary, but its whole-set target is distinct from pointwise validification; by itself it is too thin and is retained only inside the computational kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected as a standalone projection-only paper.

seed_details.seed: critical invalidity budget for sign reversal
seed_details.kernel: Along a prespecified nested path of thresholds and counts, characterize the smallest budget at which zero enters the entire-set confidence complex and certify all discontinuous assignment changes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: VIPER's scalar widening path must be replaced by a partially ordered family of count-and-magnitude budgets with discontinuous quota optimizers.
seed_details.red_team: A robustness value is just a one-dimensional search over the existing confidence set.
seed_details.rebuttal: Nested count budgets are not totally ordered without a declared path, and an exact critical value requires the same exchange-cycle algebra plus a new bivariate parameter partition.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A prespecified path and named critical budget avoid a qualitative sensitivity-only claim.

seed_details.kernel: Show that uniform whole-set coverage over a class of nonzero local first stages forces unbounded output with positive probability after every quota-admissible trimming choice.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Dufour's one-parameter local nonidentification sequence must be made compatible with a common nested budget across the finite union of admissible assignments.
seed_details.red_team: A direct specialization of Dufour's 1997 impossibility theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: The quota-union construction is nontrivial but does not generalize Dufour; the result is supporting theory rather than the headline.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: No flagship claim is made for a comparator specialization.

seed_details.kernel: Prove exact equivariance of costs, covariance blocks, roots, rays, and component labels under all SNP sign actions, then reassess the 48 published risk-factor--disease pairs.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Population absolute-magnitude invariance must be lifted through covariance-aware finite-sample projection and certified topology output.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate because absolute values erase every sign flip.
seed_details.rebuttal: Residuals, covariance representations, root labels, and software output must transform coherently, but the theorem is still secondary once the envelope is explicit.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is group equivariance, not mislabeled permutation inference.

seed_details.seed: whole-set VIPER validification over quota unions
seed_details.kernel: Replace pointwise probability-integral-transform validification by an exactly calibrated supremum event covering every effect compatible with a nested quota union.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The pointwise calibration probability must be uniformized over the flat-top identified set before profiling over the nonconvex violation union.
seed_details.red_team: Strong validity of the possibility contour already implies coverage for all compatible effects.
seed_details.rebuttal: VIPER's Corollary 1 quantifies over data-generating parameters one at a time; it does not control the intersection of coverage events for every effect compatible with one reduced form.
seed_details.disposition: credible but deferred in favor of the transparent joint-ellipsoid event
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The target is explicitly simultaneous rather than a pointwise relabeling.

seed_details.kernel: Match an upper and lower rate for Hausdorff and component recovery as \(p\) grows under a separation margin.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: The fixed-dimensional exact envelope would need empirical-process control over a growing combinatorial assignment class and a least-favorable topology-collision experiment.
seed_details.red_team: The proposed assumptions would encode the desired separation rate and make the converse tautological.
seed_details.rebuttal: The search found no primitive class that avoids that defect while preserving the BudgetIV target, so this seed is dropped rather than padded.
seed_details.disposition: dropped after named M11(a) search obstruction
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected because a rate dictated by an assumed separation margin would assume the answer.

seed_details.seed: semiparametric efficiency for regular BudgetIV endpoints
seed_details.kernel: Derive an efficiency bound for the vector of regular separated endpoints and an attaining estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: One would need the tangent space of the summary-data law and an influence function for the active ratio endpoints.
seed_details.red_team: On a stable face the endpoint is a smooth ratio, so the parametric Gaussian efficiency bound is routine.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in the fixed-known-covariance experiment; the seed is dropped, while the nontrivial outward confidence-endpoint limit is retained under M11(c).
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Rejected as a routine influence-function calculation on a self-selected regular stratum.

seed_details.kernel: Choose pleiotropy budgets data-adaptively to minimize a regret criterion.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A causal welfare target and oracle policy class would have to be defined separately from the analyst's identifying assumptions.
seed_details.red_team: A budget is a sensitivity assumption, not a treatment policy, so welfare regret is the wrong object.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; no defensible causal-policy consumer was found, so the mandatory M16 lane is documented and dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Not converted into a pseudo-policy merely to satisfy motif diversity.

seed_details.kernel: Use the SNP sign group as a randomization orbit to calibrate exact confidence sets.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: A valid exchangeability law for observed allele orientations would be required before sign-orbit p-values could be inverted.
seed_details.red_team: Allele recoding is deterministic reparameterization, not sampling symmetry, so its orbit is not a randomization distribution.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds; the honest result is deterministic equivariance, retained as seed 7, not M17 coverage.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: No exchangeability assumption is invented to turn coding invariance into permutation inference.

literature_map.anchor_read: Penn et al. (2025), Introduction, Sections 3--4, inference section, coverage theorem, and Discussion; the paper establishes sharp nested-budget identification, polynomial scalar population computation, and asymptotic NOME coverage, while explicitly leaving non-NOME coverage open.
adjacent_threads: Dufour and Taamouti (2005), Introduction and quadric projection theorems: finite-sample pivotal projection and boundedness for ordinary weak-IV quadrics.
Wang and Kang (2022), Theorem 1: two-sample summary-data AR, Kleibergen, and CLR null limits under weak first stages in the disjoint exposure--outcome submodel represented here by \(B_j=0\).
Kang et al. (2022), Section 3 and Theorem 1: count-invalid subset-union confidence intervals with pointwise effect coverage.
Schlemper and Moreira (2026), Introduction, Sections 4--7, and Conclusion: exact polynomial and rational inversion for ordinary weak-IV statistics and documented grid omissions.
Steiner, Houssineau, and Steel (2026), Proposition 1, Proposition 2, Corollary 1, Appendix A, and Conclusion: projection onto violation sets followed by exact pointwise validification.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: Projection, pointwise finite-sample validity, subset unions, and ordinary root inversion are occupied separately. No opened source supplies the nested-quota min-cost envelope, exchange-cycle completeness, certified full topology, and simultaneous population-set containment in one theorem.

literature_map.anchor_read: Fieller (1954), ratio-root construction and Gaussian quadratic classification; Penn et al. (2025), scalar disconnected-set construction and inference discussion.
adjacent_threads: Mikusheva (2010), Introduction and confidence-set-shape results: honest weak-IV sets can be infinite and require complete inversion.
Dufour (1997), main impossibility result: a valid set for an unbounded locally almost unidentified parameter must be unbounded with positive probability.
Schlemper and Moreira (2026), ray recovery by polynomial leading behavior and cellwise sign determination.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: Single-statistic leading-coefficient tail tests are occupied. The exact quota-trimmed limit and ordered lower-coefficient resolution at \(L=q\) are not found in these sources.

literature_map.candidate: regular-face endpoint and label limit law
literature_map.anchor_read: Penn et al. (2025), scalar algorithm and Discussion: disconnected components carry assignment interpretations, but no endpoint limit or label-recovery theorem is given.
adjacent_threads: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007), criterion-contour framework: whole-set estimation, convergence rates, and confidence regions without labeled disconnected-boundary recovery.
Gafarov (2025), regularized support-function theorem and Conclusion: Gaussian limits under regular affine geometry and consistency under nonregularity.
Fang and Santos (2019), main bootstrap theorem: full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for ordinary bootstrap consistency under Gaussian limits.
Hirano and Porter (2012), main impossibility result: nondifferentiable targets preclude regular locally unbiased estimation.
literature_map.occupancy_conclusion: General regular and directional limit theory is occupied, but the outward-shifted joint endpoint vector and probability-one recovery of BudgetIV component pairings and tier labels on separated faces are not stated in the opened literature.

novelty_justification: The closest published source, Penn et al. (2025), owns the nested budget and sharp disconnected population set and already sketches asymptotic whole-set uncertainty under NOME. The closest current computational source, Schlemper and Moreira (2026), owns root-based inversion of a fixed rational or polynomial weak-IV statistic. The closest current finite-sample invalid-IV source, VIPER (2026), owns exact pointwise validification for one true effect under a posited violation set. The field-level strict delta is the quota-flow exchange-cycle completeness and equality-complete topology inversion: the exact graded-quota projection is a balanced min-cost flow, every optimizer transition is captured by a polynomial-size fixed-\(K\) exchange family, and certified sign decomposition returns the entire topology. Whole-set Gaussian coverage supports that kernel only inside the fixed-dimensional block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment with known covariance; \(B_j\ne0\) represents correlated or overlapping exposure--outcome summaries, while independent disjoint two-sample summaries impose \(B_j=0\). The trimmed-tail iff and regular-face joint limit are consequential topology theorems enabled by the envelope. The proposal explicitly disclaims superiority to Anderson--Rubin or conditional likelihood ratio procedures on the all-valid submodel, restricts Fieller quadratic inversion to \(p=1\), and treats Dufour's impossibility as inherited supporting logic.
message: Revised the full core to define a block-independent paired-summary exact Gaussian experiment, permit known nonzero within-pair covariance for correlated or overlapping summaries, and identify independent disjoint two-sample GWAS as the B_j=0 submodel. Preserved all prior scope caveats and the quota-flow certified-inversion kernel. JSON schema, proposal gate, symbol/dependency audit, terminology audit, and LaTeX compilation pass.
